title: An acknowledgement lost in a tunnel
description: Alice sends a message, the server persists it as sequence 1043, and her phone loses connectivity before receiving the acknowledgement. It retries the same clientMsgId after reconnecting. Meanwhile, Bob has sent another message from a different gateway. How should the conversation owner handle Alice's retry?

options.text: Return Alice's original sequence using the sender/clientMsgId mapping, without appending another message.
options.explanation: The original durable message already has its place in the conversation order. Reusing the acknowledgement makes the retry idempotent while Bob's distinct send gets its own sequence.

options.text: Append Alice's retry with a new sequence so acknowledgements always refer to the latest request.
options.explanation: That turns a network retry into a duplicate visible message. Request attempts are not separate user messages.

options.text: Reorder Alice's retry before Bob's message using Alice's phone timestamp.
options.explanation: Phone clocks cannot establish the shared order, and rewriting the order after delivery makes devices disagree.

options.text: Drop all of Alice's sends until every member confirms receipt of sequence 1043.
options.explanation: One offline member would block the conversation. Durable server acknowledgement and per-device sync avoid that dependency.
